text: I'm bullish BTC here at 84k. BTC's shown strength in the middle of the 10y spiralling, war increase and oil spikes Im in about a 8 or 9/10 confidence that we've flipped to a bullish regime, the 82k level isn't something that's broken like it was without serious smart money backing the move. As someone who was here every second of the 2023 bear, i'm seeing a lot of parallels and typical disbelief type personas. You need this for the next legs higher, consensus won't properly change until we're around the 100k level again and every agrees we're "officially back", until then its a slow grind with lots of commentary from people who haven't had multiple cycles. At the same time I can recognise crypto is in a fairly neutral position even after breaking key resistance. There's still plenty of variables that can drive us down such as inflation/bonds, war, AI security risks, mid terms etc, however negative news has continued having minimal impact on price which has always been the strongest indicator. Positive news turns crypto into the highest beta asset and we've finally entered outperformance for the first time in 12 months. As we come into mid terms and Anthropic IPO, it's a pretty safe to assume Trump will be doing the hard yards to keep things afloat. You can also see Dario's in the cuck chair from his body language in a recent interview with him, Trump, Zuck and other leaders. I don't think Anthropic will be pulling any "power" moves against the government. Regarding onchain, my thoughts haven't changed much from my previous post: Essentially been a crab market due to innovation exemption and froth across leading chains/launchpads. As I mentioned, these are one of the scenarios with onchain that it's better to be late than early to buying the dip/reversal. Normally I attempt to catch pico bottoms with onchain and play into my intuition + data analysis from monitoring responses to events by a pool of individuals, although the catalyst that drove us down puts thick clouds over the eco which can't be removed without more clarification. It's an uphill battle for most coins to perform here until tokenized stocks are green lighted for permissionless trading + 1:1 redemptions and voting, unless fundamentals significantly improve to respark momentum. Traders are also becoming too dependant on the Vlad effect, there needs to be natural discovery and interest for narratives otherwise he'll burn the wick if eco's are solely reliant on him. Atm there's strong fatigue and hangover across the board, causing uncertainty for people willing to buy in with conviction. Yes this marks bottoms eventually, but in this case it also drags out a crab market for onchain. From experience, I find it much easier timing bottoms as it's generally a more predictable and visible emotion of disparity towards the environment (traders hating on launchpads, victim mentality, hindsight bias, lack of confidence etc). When we enter this style of crab, the reversal is much more gradual and you need to read between the lines of subtle shifts, such as novel tech rekindling excitement and higher lows for leading coins. Onchain has led majors like we expected since end of June, BTC and majority of alts haven't had much of a moment yet. Even while onchain has mostly decoupled from majors, BTC having strength here over the next week or two will add a lot of confidence to our bags. Current projections are BTC chopping around at this 82-87k level for 4-7 days, BTC dominance remains fairly strong while leading alts continue to cool off a little. Onchain more or less the same in a crab market. Once we start breaking 87k, pay very close attention to how leading coins are moving, even if there's regulatory overcast, traders will look to front run any potential positive outcomes.

text: Highlight Clip: THORChain's "Decentralization" Faces Scrutiny After Bitget Asks It to Block Hackers THORChain's "Decentralization" Faces Scrutiny After Bitget Asks It to Block Hackers Bitget CEO Gracy Chen asked THORChain to refuse service to publicly identified attacker addresses, saying decentralization should not be a shield for facilitating stolen funds. THORChain emphasized that its network is permissionless. In May 2026, an attack on one of THORChain's vaults caused approximately $10.7 million in losses. Automatic safeguards and coordinated action by node operators subsequently halted the network. Co-founder Chad Barraford later discussed ideas for anomaly detection and emergency pauses on a podcast, outlining security checks and asset migration procedures before trading could resume. While halting a network is not the same as freezing specific addresses, the dispute raises a question: Under what circumstances should a decentralized protocol intervene when stolen funds originate from an external platform? — link
